focus: 'too' /tuː/ vs weak 'to' /tə/ · 'enough' /ɪˈnʌf/ stress + position · 'a bit / a little' weak rhythm · degree phrase linking · 'not enough' vs 'too much'
focus_ar: الفرق بين 'too' القوية و 'to' الخفيفة، ونبر 'enough' وموضعها، وإيقاع 'a bit / a little'، وربط عبارات الدرجة
arabic_challenge: 'too' (=زيادة عن اللازم) sounds almost like weak 'to', but they mean different things and 'too' is stressed. 'enough' comes AFTER adjectives but BEFORE nouns, and its stress is on the second syllable. Arabic learners flatten 'a bit' and confuse 'too much' with 'very'.

isolation.instructions: 'too' means 'more than we want' and is STRESSED with a long /uː/: 'too HOT', 'too EXPENSIVE'. It is NOT the same as 'very'. Say the long vowel clearly.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'too' معناها 'أكثر من اللازم' ومنبورة بحرف /uː/ طويل: 'too HOT'. مش نفس 'very'.

sentence_practice: The bag is too heavy for me.
It's too late to call him now.
daily_drills.record_this: This coffee is too hot to drink right now. The bag is too heavy for me to carry. It's too late to call him tonight, so I'll message him tomorrow.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'too hot'. Is 'too' stressed with a long /uː/, meaning 'more than you want'?

isolation.instructions: In 'too ADJ to VERB', the first word 'too' is strong /tuː/ and the second word 'to' is weak /tə/: 'too TIRED tə WALK'. Two spellings that sound different — feel the contrast.
isolation.instructions_ar: في 'too ADJ to VERB': الأولى 'too' قوية /tuː/ والثانية 'to' خفيفة /tə/: 'too TIRED tə WALK'.

sentence_practice: I'm too tired to walk home.
He's too young to drive a car.
It's too dark to see anything.
daily_drills.record_this: I'm too tired to walk home, so I'll take a taxi. He's too young to drive a car legally. The room was too dark to see anything, so we turned on the lights.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'too tired to walk'. Is the first 'too' strong /tuː/ and the second 'to' weak /tə/?

isolation.instructions: 'enough' is stressed on the SECOND syllable /ɪˈnʌf/ and ends in an /f/ sound. Position: it comes AFTER an adjective ('big ENOUGH') but BEFORE a noun ('enough TIME'). Say it clearly.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'enough' منبورة على المقطع الثاني /ɪˈnʌf/ وتنتهي بـ /f/. تأتي بعد الصفة ('big enough') وقبل الاسم ('enough time').

daily_drills.record_this: This room isn't big enough for the party. We don't have enough time to finish today. Are you warm enough, or shall I close the window? He's old enough to decide for himself.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'big enough' then 'enough time'. Is stress on the second syllable /ɪˈnʌf/, and is the position correct (after adjective, before noun)?

isolation.instructions: 'a bit' and 'a little' soften an adjective and are said quickly as one light group: 'ə bit TIRED', 'ə little COLD'. The adjective is stressed; the softener is weak and fast.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'a bit' و 'a little' تخفّف الصفة وتُقال بسرعة كمجموعة خفيفة: 'ə bit TIRED'. الصفة منبورة والمخفّف خفيف.

sentence_practice: It's a little cold in here.
Can I have a bit of help?
daily_drills.record_this: I'm a bit tired today, but I'm fine. It's a little cold in here — could you close the door? The food was a bit expensive, but it was delicious. Can I have a little help with this?
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'a bit tired'. Is 'a bit' light and fast, with the stress on the adjective?

target_sounds: degree phrase linking (too/enough/a bit in flow)

isolation.instructions: Put the pieces together in real speech: 'It's a bit too expensive', 'not warm enough', 'too far to walk'. Keep 'too' strong, 'enough' second-syllable stressed, and softeners weak — all linked smoothly.
isolation.instructions_ar: اجمع القطع في كلام حقيقي: 'a bit too expensive'، 'not warm enough'. حافظ على 'too' قوية و'enough' منبورة وخفّف المخفّفات.

sentence_practice: It's a bit too expensive for me.
There were too many people there.
daily_drills.record_this: This jacket is a bit too expensive for me right now. The soup isn't warm enough — could you heat it up? There were too many people at the station, and not enough time to catch the train.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'a bit too expensive'. Are 'too' strong, 'enough' second-syllable stressed, and the softeners weak, all linked smoothly?

challenge_sentences: This coffee is too hot to drink.
The room isn't big enough for everyone.
I'm a bit tired, but I'm fine.
There were too many people and not enough chairs.
daily_drills.record_this: This coffee is too hot to drink right now, so I'll wait. The room isn't big enough for everyone, so some people are standing. I'm a bit tired today, but honestly I'm fine. At the party there were too many people and not enough chairs.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: strong 'too' /tuː/ vs weak 'to' /tə/, correct 'enough' stress and position, and light 'a bit / a little'.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself describing a place or plan using degree words, then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تصف مكانًا أو خطة مستخدمًا كلمات الدرجة، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل نقطة.
test_yourself.passage: Let me tell you why we didn't enjoy that restaurant. First, it was a bit too far to walk, so we had to take a taxi. When we arrived, it was too crowded and there weren't enough tables, so we waited a long time. The food was good, but the portions weren't big enough, and the prices were far too high for what we got. My friend said the music was a little too loud to have a real conversation. Honestly, it was too expensive to go there again. Next time we'll choose somewhere close enough to walk, quiet enough to talk, and cheap enough for students like us.

sounds_to_check.strong 'too' /tuː/: too far, too crowded, too high, too loud, too expensive
sounds_to_check.weak 'to' /tə/ after too: too far tə walk, too loud tə talk, too expensive tə go
sounds_to_check.'enough' stress + position: enough tables, big enough, close enough, quiet enough, cheap enough
sounds_to_check.weak softeners: a bit too far, a little too loud
sounds_to_check.count vs uncount: not enough tables, prices too high

scoring_guide.90_100: Clear 'too' vs 'to', correct 'enough' stress/position, light softeners. Ready for week 14.
scoring_guide.70_89: Good; occasional flat 'a bit' or misplaced 'enough'.
scoring_guide.50_69: 'too' and 'to' sound the same, or 'enough big'. Repeat days 1-3.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, keeping 'too' strong and 'enough' after adjectives / before nouns.

for_arabic_speakers: 'too' = more than you want (a problem); 'very' = just a high degree (not a problem). They are different.
'too' is strong /tuː/; the linking 'to' before a verb is weak /tə/ — same spelling family, different sound.
'enough' is stressed on the second syllable and goes AFTER adjectives but BEFORE nouns.
'a bit / a little' are soft and fast; the stress stays on the adjective they soften.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
